summary: This step built the one normalized record every model in the zoo reads: 39,286 rows, one per allele, each carrying the genomic change, the transcript, the protein change (`hgvs_p`, the standard spelling for 'this amino acid became that one'), and the coordinate kept in a separate column so the record itself stays coordinate-free. It ran one Ensembl VEP (Variant Effect Predictor, the tool that turns a raw coordinate into gene/transcript/protein consequences) REST pass over 196 batches, checkpointed so a crash costs one batch, finishing in 1 h 45 m. 38,069 of 38,087 coding alleles (99.953%) got a usable spelling. Two problems surfaced mid-run: Ensembl's POST endpoint 500s on `uniprot=1` (so every record's `uniprot` field is null, deferred to step 2), and `BUB1B`, the gene behind the confirmed compound-heterozygous pair, carries one missense and one stop-gained allele — a consequence class three of the four planned model lanes cannot score at all.
why: Every model class downstream reads a different slice of the same allele — a genomic coordinate, a transcript-relative change, a protein substitution, a DNA or protein window — and without one record holding all of them, each model lane would need its own ad-hoc lookup, with no shared key to join scores back together or trace where a number came from. Skipping this step would mean the zoo registry (step 2) has nothing to fetch coverage against, and no adapter could promise it scores 'the record set' rather than some private list of variants.
verdict: H058 (`P4-1a`) supported at confidence 0.95: 99.953% of coding alleles got a non-null `hgvs_c` or `hgvs_p`, comfortably over the 99% bar. The run also surfaced a structural gap it did not set out to test: the confirmed pair's stop-gained half sits in a consequence class most planned lanes cannot score, flagged as risk R9 and left for step 2 as GPN-MSA's promotion, not fixed here.

inherits.what: Nothing inside iteration 4 — this is the first step. It reads four source tables from the warehouse (the shared database every iteration draws from) directly, which is why its lineage edge names all four rather than pointing at another iteration-4 step.

hands_to.what: The 39,286-record set is the only thing step 2's registry can measure coverage against — 'AlphaMissense covers 27.0% of records' is meaningless without a fixed denominator. Step 2 also inherits the open uniprot problem directly: ESM1b's adapter has to build its own `ENSP` (Ensembl protein id) to UniProt accession map because this step's join left that column null.
